title: Chiral carbon atoms
keyIdea: A chiral carbon is bonded to four different groups. A molecule with one chiral carbon has two forms that are mirror images but cannot be superimposed, however you turn them. These two forms are enantiomers, a type of optical isomer. Swapping any two groups turns one enantiomer into the other. Enantiomers rotate plane-polarised light by the same angle in opposite directions, so a 50:50 racemic mixture shows no rotation.

kid: A carbon atom makes four bonds. They point to the corners of a tetrahedron. If all four groups on a carbon are different, the carbon is chiral. In butan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, the second carbon holds H, OH, CH₃ and C₂H₅. All four differ, so it is chiral. Compare whole groups, not just the first atom.

A chiral molecule has a mirror image that will not fit on top of it. Your hands work the same way. Turn the mirror image any way you like. At best two of the four groups line up. The two forms are called enantiomers. They are a type of optical isomer.

To draw the pair in 3D, put two bonds in the page. Draw one as a wedge, which points towards you. Draw one as a dashed line, which points away. Then draw the mirror image beside it. If you swap any two groups, you get the other enantiomer.

Enantiomers have the same boiling point and the same formula. One big difference is how they treat plane-polarised light. One form turns it clockwise. The other turns it the same angle anticlockwise. A 50:50 mix is called racemic. The two turns cancel, so the light comes out unturned.
adult: This A-level chemistry topic (ages 17 to 18) covers optical isomerism. A carbon bonded to four different groups is a chiral centre, also called an asymmetric carbon or stereocentre. A molecule with one such centre exists as two non-superimposable mirror images, called enantiomers. Students mark the chiral carbon, draw both enantiomers with wedge and dash bonds, and explain why they cannot be superimposed. It builds on tetrahedral shape, structural formulae and isomerism.

The test is about groups, not atoms. In pentan-3-ol, the middle carbon holds H, OH and two ethyl groups. Two groups match, so it is not chiral, even though the atoms next to it look varied. Enantiomers share physical properties such as melting point. They rotate plane-polarised light equally in opposite directions. They can also act differently with other chiral molecules, such as receptors and enzymes. (R)-carvone smells of spearmint; (S)-carvone smells of caraway.

Common mistakes: calling any carbon with an OH or a halogen chiral; comparing only the attached atoms, not whole groups; counting a C=O carbon, which has only three groups; drawing the mirror image with the same wedge pattern, which gives the same molecule; and saying a racemic mixture rotates light. Be careful when you swap groups. One swap gives the other enantiomer, but two swaps give the first one back.

The lab has five parts. You tap the chiral carbon in four molecules, or say there is none. You build a centre, then break its chirality with one change. You turn a 3D mirror image of butan-2-ol and find that only two of its four groups ever line up. You swap two groups and make it fit. Last, you mix two enantiomers in a polarimeter until the rotation cancels.

familyTip: Ask your teenager to hold up both hands, palms down, and try to lay one exactly on the other. Then ask them to name a molecule that works the same way, and to say which carbon makes it so.

practice.prompt: Which carbon in butan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, is chiral?
choices: C2, the carbon with the OH
C1, the CH₃ at the end
C3, the CH₂
practice.hint: List the four groups on each carbon and look for four different ones.
practice.explain: C2 holds H, OH, CH₃ and C₂H₅: four different groups. C1 has three H atoms and C3 has two.

practice.prompt: The pure (+) enantiomer rotates plane-polarised light {a}° clockwise. At the same concentration, how many degrees anticlockwise does the pure (−) enantiomer rotate it?
practice.hint: Enantiomers rotate light by the same angle in opposite directions.

practice.prompt: Is the central carbon in propan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₃, chiral?
choices: No, it has two CH₃ groups
Yes, it has an OH group
Yes, every central carbon is chiral
practice.hint: Write out its four groups: H, OH and what else?
practice.explain: Its groups are H, OH, CH₃ and CH₃. Two match, so it is not chiral and has no enantiomers.

practice.prompt: A sample is {a}% of one enantiomer and {=100-a}% of the other. What percentage of the sample is a racemic 50:50 pair?
practice.hint: Each molecule of the minor form pairs with one of the major form.
practice.explain: The {=100-a}% minor form pairs with {=100-a}% of the major form, so {=2*(100-a)}% is racemic. The rest gives the rotation.

practice.prompt: You swap two groups on one enantiomer of a chiral molecule. What do you get?
choices: The other enantiomer
The same molecule
A molecule that is not chiral
practice.hint: Think about what the lab showed when you swapped two groups on the mirror image.
practice.explain: One swap gives the mirror image, the other enantiomer. A second swap gives the first back.

pool.prompt: Which molecule contains a chiral carbon?
choices: CH₃CHClCH₂CH₃
CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂Cl
CH₃CHClCH₃
pool.hint: Find a carbon holding H, Cl and two different carbon groups.
pool.explain: In 2-chlorobutane, C2 holds H, Cl, CH₃ and C₂H₅. In 2-chloropropane the CHCl carbon has two CH₃ groups.

pool.prompt: Is C3 in pentan-3-ol, CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, chiral?
choices: No, it holds two ethyl groups
Yes, it holds four different atoms
Yes, it holds an OH group
pool.hint: Compare whole groups, not just the atoms attached.
pool.explain: C3 holds H, OH, C₂H₅ and C₂H₅. Two groups are the same, so it is not chiral.

pool.prompt: The pure (S) form of a compound rotates light {a}° anticlockwise. How many degrees clockwise does the pure (R) form rotate it, at the same concentration?
pool.hint: The two enantiomers rotate by equal amounts in opposite directions.

choices: A 50:50 mix of two enantiomers, with no net rotation
A pure enantiomer that rotates light strongly
A mix of two structural isomers
pool.hint: Think about what the polarimeter showed at 50:50.
pool.explain: Equal amounts of each enantiomer rotate light equally in opposite directions, so the rotations cancel.

pool.prompt: How many chiral carbons are in alanine, CH₃CH(NH₂)COOH?
pool.hint: The COOH carbon has a C=O double bond. How many groups does that leave it?
pool.explain: The CH carbon holds H, NH₂, CH₃ and COOH. The COOH carbon has only three groups, and the CH₃ has three H atoms.

pool.prompt: A sample is {a}% (+) form and the rest is (−) form. By how many percentage points does (+) exceed (−)?
pool.hint: First find the percentage of the (−) form: 100 − {a}.
pool.explain: (−) is {=100-a}%, so (+) exceeds it by {a} − {=100-a} = {=2*a-100} points. Only this excess rotates light.

pool.prompt: Why can two enantiomers never be superimposed?
choices: They are mirror images of a carbon with four different groups
They have different molecular formulas
Their bonds are different lengths
pool.hint: Recall the mirror step: at best only two of the four groups lined up.
pool.explain: With four different groups, no rotation maps the mirror image onto the original. They have the same formula and bonds.

pool.prompt: (R)-carvone smells of spearmint and (S)-carvone of caraway. What explains this?
choices: Smell receptors are chiral, so each enantiomer fits differently
The two forms have different boiling points
The two forms have different formulas
pool.hint: Enantiomers act differently only with polarised light and with other chiral things.
pool.explain: Receptor proteins are chiral, like a left glove. Each enantiomer fits them in a different way.

visual.caption: Is the marked carbon chiral? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: C2 of butan-2-ol: H, OH, CH₃, C₂H₅
C2 of propan-2-ol: H, OH, CH₃, CH₃
C2 of lactic acid: H, OH, CH₃, COOH
C3 of pentan-3-ol: H, OH, C₂H₅, C₂H₅
C2 of 2-chlorobutane: H, Cl, CH₃, C₂H₅

lab.caption: Flagship lab: tap the chiral carbon, build and break a chiral centre, turn a 3D mirror image, swap two groups, and cancel rotation in a polarimeter.
